title: Two massive baby stars may have become a binary after forming separately
freshness: Published in Nature Astronomy on 7 September 2026, within the 15-day freshness window.
excerpt: Astronomers followed two massive baby stars and found that their stretched orbit and tilted surrounding disks are hard to explain if the stars were born together. The evidence instead suggests they formed separately, passed close to one another, and became gravitationally bound as a pair.
whyItMatters: Most massive stars live with a stellar companion, but scientists still do not fully understand how those partnerships begin. This result suggests that some massive binary stars may form through a later gravitational encounter, adding a new route to the story of how the biggest stars are born and evolve.
